ei.title: Little William and the Meatball Vendor

fullPassage:
(A) One evening, little William was on his way home from his friend's. He was passing through the market. On his way, he came across the beautiful aroma of some meatballs sold by an elderly vendor just across the road. The smell was so pleasant that little William had to stop by the stand to purchase some meatballs. However, the meatballs didn't have a listed price, so he decided to head directly home. Just as little William turned to leave, a firm voice stopped (a) him.

(B) The shopkeeper angrily shouted, "When did you pay the money? You reached into your pocket but came out empty-handed!" Little William made it clear that he had just paid, reminding the shopkeeper that he had heard the jingle of the coins from his pocket. (b) He added that if smelling is as good as eating, then hearing the sound of the coins should also be as good as receiving them. He smiled proudly and walked home from there, leaving the man completely surprised.

(C) It was the elderly vendor. "Wait! You can't just leave. Before you go, you have to pay," he said. Little William was surprised at the statement made by the elderly vendor. (c) He asked him, "Payment for what, Sir? I didn't purchase any meatballs." The vendor insisted that although little William did not purchase any meatballs, he enjoyed the pleasant smell of his meatballs for quite a long time. (d) He truly believed that little William had to pay for it because smelling was as good as eating.

(D) Little William was upset about this. He didn't know how merely smelling the meatballs meant that (e) he had to pay for them. After observing the man for a short while, little William dipped his hands in his pocket and jingled a few coins. The elderly vendor was excited to hear the coin sound. He said, "Now hurry up, boy. Pay the money fast." Little William replied, "I have already paid the money, Sir. You didn't understand?"

questions.passage: One evening, little William was on his way home from his friend's. On his way, he came across the beautiful (A)[aroma / noise] of some meatballs sold by an elderly (B)[vendor / customer] just across the road. The smell was so (C)[pleasant / terrible] that little William had to stop by the stand.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 미트볼의 아름다운 향기(aroma)가 났고, 노점 상인(vendor)이 팔고 있었으며, 냄새가 너무 좋아서(pleasant) 멈춰야 했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① aroma — vendor — pleasant: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ② noise(소음): 향기가 아닌 소음
❌ ③ customer(손님): 파는 사람은 vendor
❌ ④ terrible(끔찍한): pleasant의 반의어
det.tip: aroma(향기), vendor(상인), pleasant(기분 좋은) — 시장 장면의 핵심 어휘

questions.passage: The vendor insisted that although little William did not purchase any meatballs, he (A)[enjoyed / avoided] the pleasant smell for quite a long time. He truly (B)[believed / doubted] that little William had to pay for it because smelling was as good as (C)[eating / cooking].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: William이 향기를 즐겼고(enjoyed), 상인은 냄새 맡는 것이 먹는 것만큼이라고 진심으로 믿었으며(believed), 냄새가 먹는 것(eating)만큼 좋다고 했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① enjoyed — believed — eating: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ② avoided(피했다): enjoyed의 반의어
❌ ③ doubted(의심했다): believed의 반의어
❌ ④ cooking(요리): eating이 원문
det.tip: smelling is as good as eating: 냄새 맡기 = 먹기 — 상인의 논리

questions.passage: After observing the man for a short while, little William dipped his hands in his pocket and (A)[jingled / dropped] a few coins. The elderly vendor was (B)[excited / disappointed] to hear the coin sound. Little William replied, "I have already paid the money, Sir." He smiled (C)[proudly / nervously] and walked home, leaving the man completely surprised.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: William은 동전을 쨍그랑 흔들었고(jingled), 상인은 소리에 흥분했으며(excited), William은 자랑스럽게(proudly) 웃으며 집에 갔습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ jingled — excited — proudly: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ① dropped(떨어뜨렸다): jingled(흔들었다)와 다른 행동
❌ ② disappointed(실망한): excited(흥분한)의 반의어
❌ ④ nervously(긴장하며): proudly(자랑스럽게)의 반의어
det.tip: jingled(쨍그랑 소리를 내다) — William의 기지 있는 반격의 핵심 행동

questions.passage: One evening, little William was on his way home from his friend's. He came across the beautiful aroma of some meatballs sold by an elderly vendor. The smell was so ①<u>pleasant</u> that little William had to stop by the stand. However, the meatballs didn't have a ②<u>listed</u> price, so he decided to head directly home. Just as little William turned to leave, a ③<u>gentle</u> voice stopped him. It was the elderly vendor. "Wait! You can't just leave. Before you go, you have to ④<u>pay</u>," he said.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①②④는 원문과 일치합니다. ③gentle(부드러운)은 원문의 firm(단호한)을 반의어로 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②④: 원문 그대로
❌ ③ gentle(부드러운) → firm(단호한): '멈춰!'라고 세게 말하는 맥락에서 단호한 목소리
det.tip: firm(단호한) ↔ gentle(부드러운): 상인이 William을 멈추는 강한 어조

questions.passage: Little William was ①<u>upset</u> about this. He didn't know how merely smelling the meatballs meant that he had to pay for them. After ②<u>observing</u> the man for a short while, little William dipped his hands in his pocket and ③<u>jingled</u> a few coins. The elderly vendor was excited to hear the coin sound. Little William replied, "I have already paid the money, Sir." He smiled ④<u>sheepishly</u> and walked home from there, leaving the man completely surprised.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①②③은 원문과 일치합니다. ④sheepishly(쑥스럽게)는 원문의 proudly(자랑스럽게)를 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②③: 원문 그대로
❌ ④ sheepishly(쑥스럽게) → proudly(자랑스럽게): 기지 있는 반격에 자신감 있는 미소
det.tip: proudly(자랑스럽게) ↔ sheepishly(쑥스럽게): William의 승리감 표현

questions.passage: The shopkeeper angrily shouted, "When did you pay the money? You reached into your pocket but came out ①<u>empty-handed</u>!" Little William made it ②<u>clear</u> that he had just paid, reminding the shopkeeper that he had heard the ③<u>jingle</u> of the coins from his pocket. He added that if smelling is as good as eating, then hearing the sound of the coins should also be as good as ④<u>spending</u> them.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①②③은 원문과 일치합니다. ④spending(쓰는 것)은 원문의 receiving(받는 것)을 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②③: 원문 그대로
❌ ④ spending(쓰는 것) → receiving(받는 것): 동전 소리 듣기 = 돈 '받기'라는 논리
det.tip: receiving(받는 것) ≠ spending(쓰는 것): William의 논리는 smelling:eating = hearing:receiving

questions.passage: One evening, little William was on his way home from his friend's. He was passing through the market. On his way, he came across the beautiful aroma of some meatballs sold by an elderly vendor just across the road. The smell was so pleasant that little William had to stop by the stand to purchase some meatballs. However, the meatballs didn't have a listed price, so he decided to head directly home. Just as little William turned to leave, a __________ voice stopped him.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: William이 떠나려 할 때 단호한(firm) 목소리가 그를 멈추게 했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ firm(단호한): '멈춰! 떠날 수 없어'라는 강한 어조
❌ ① soft(부드러운): 단호한 제지와 맞지 않음
❌ ② cheerful(쾌활한): 상인의 요구 맥락과 불일치
❌ ③ hesitant(망설이는): 확고한 제지와 반대
det.tip: firm voice = 단호한 목소리. 상인이 William을 강하게 제지하는 장면

questions.passage: Little William was upset about this. He didn't know how merely smelling the meatballs meant that he had to pay for them. After observing the man for a short while, little William dipped his hands in his pocket and jingled a few coins. The elderly vendor was excited to hear the coin sound. He said, "Now hurry up, boy. Pay the money fast." Little William replied, "I have already paid the money, Sir. You didn't __________?"
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: William은 '이미 돈을 냈다'며 상인에게 '이해하지 못했느냐(understand)'고 물었습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② understand(이해하다): 동전 소리 = 지불이라는 논리를 이해하지 못함
❌ ① agree(동의하다): 이해 여부를 묻는 것
❌ ③ forget(잊다): 방금 일어난 일
❌ ④ notice(알아채다): 소리를 들었으므로 알아챔
det.tip: You didn't understand? = 이해 못 하셨나요? William의 기지 있는 반격

questions.passage: The shopkeeper angrily shouted, "When did you pay the money? You reached into your pocket but came out empty-handed!" Little William made it clear that he had just paid, reminding the shopkeeper that he had heard the jingle of the coins from his pocket. He added that if smelling is as good as eating, then hearing the sound of the coins should also be as good as __________ them.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 냄새 맡기가 먹기만큼이면, 동전 소리 듣기도 받는 것(receiving)만큼이라는 William의 논리입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① receiving(받는 것): smelling:eating = hearing:receiving의 대칭 논리
❌ ② counting(세는 것): 논리적 대칭이 안 됨
❌ ③ stealing(훔치는 것): 부정적 의미
❌ ④ hiding(숨기는 것): 맥락과 무관
det.tip: William의 핵심 논리: smell=eat → hear=receive. 감각 경험의 대칭적 등치

questions.passage: He came across the beautiful <u>aroma</u> of some meatballs sold by an elderly vendor just across the road.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 aroma와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: aroma는 '향기'라는 뜻으로, scent(향기)와 동의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ scent(향기) ≈ aroma(향기)
❌ ① taste(맛): 후각이 아닌 미각
❌ ② sound(소리): 청각
❌ ④ texture(질감): 촉각
det.tip: aroma = scent = fragrance = smell: '향기' 동의어군

questions.passage: Little William was <u>upset</u> about this. He didn't know how merely smelling the meatballs meant that he had to pay for them.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 upset과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: upset은 '속상한, 화난'이라는 뜻으로, distressed(괴로운)와 동의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② distressed(괴로운) ≈ upset(속상한)
❌ ① excited(흥분한): 다른 감정
❌ ③ relieved(안도한): 반대 감정
❌ ④ amused(재미있어하는): 반대 감정
det.tip: upset = distressed = troubled = disturbed: '속상한' 동의어군

questions.passage: The vendor <u>insisted</u> that although little William did not purchase any meatballs, he enjoyed the pleasant smell of his meatballs for quite a long time.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 insisted와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: insisted는 '주장했다'라는 뜻으로, maintained(주장했다, 고수했다)와 동의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ maintained(주장했다) ≈ insisted(고집했다)
❌ ① whispered(속삭였다): 강하게 주장하는 것과 다름
❌ ② suggested(제안했다): 주장보다 약한 표현
❌ ③ admitted(인정했다): 주장과 다른 방향
det.tip: insisted = maintained = asserted: '강하게 주장하다' 동의어군

questions.passage: The smell was so <u>pleasant</u> that little William had to stop by the stand to purchase some meatballs.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 pleasant와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: pleasant는 '기분 좋은'이라는 뜻으로, unpleasant(불쾌한)가 반의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① unpleasant(불쾌한) ↔ pleasant(기분 좋은)
❌ ② delightful(즐거운): pleasant의 동의어
❌ ③ agreeable(마음에 드는): pleasant의 유사어
❌ ④ lovely(사랑스러운): pleasant의 유사어
det.tip: pleasant(기분 좋은) ↔ unpleasant(불쾌한): 접두사 un-으로 반의어

questions.passage: Just as little William turned to leave, a <u>firm</u> voice stopped him. It was the elderly vendor. "Wait! You can't just leave."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 firm과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: firm은 '단호한'이라는 뜻으로, hesitant(망설이는)가 반의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② hesitant(망설이는) ↔ firm(단호한)
❌ ① strong(강한): firm의 유사어
❌ ③ steady(꾸준한): firm의 유사어
❌ ④ determined(결연한): firm의 동의어
det.tip: firm(단호한) ↔ hesitant(망설이는): 확고함 vs 주저함

questions.passage:
(A) He was passing through the market. On his way, he came across the beautiful aroma of some meatballs. The meatballs didn't have a <u>listed</u> price.

(B) The building was <u>listed</u> as a national heritage site and could not be demolished.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 listed가 (A)와 (B)에서 각각 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A)에서 listed price는 표시된 가격, (B)에서 listed as는 ~로 등록된이라는 뜻입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 표시된 — (B) 등록된: 각 문맥에 정확히 부합
❌ ① (A)(B) 뒤바뀜
❌ ② 기울어진은 list(배가 기울다)의 의미
❌ ④ 나열된/기울어진은 두 문맥에 부적절
det.tip: listed: 표시된(가격)/등록된(유산)/나열된(목록)/기울어진(배) — 다의어

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어는?

"a person who sells goods, especially in the street"

det.korean: '물건을 파는 사람, 특히 거리에서 파는 사람'은 vendor(상인, 행상인)의 정의입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② vendor(행상인): 거리에서 물건 파는 사람
❌ ① customer(손님): 사는 사람
❌ ③ merchant(상인): 유사하나 규모가 더 큼
❌ ④ employer(고용주): 다른 의미
det.tip: vendor = 행상인, 노점상. especially in the street이 핵심 단서

questions.passage: One evening, little William was on his way home from his friend's. He came across the beautiful aroma of some meatballs. The smell was so pleasant that little William had to stop by the stand. However, the meatballs didn't have a listed price, so he decided to head __________ (direct) home.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: direct(형용사: 직접적인) → directly(부사: 곧바로). 동사 head를 수식하는 부사가 필요합니다.
det.analysis:
head + __________ + home 구조에서 동사를 수식하는 부사 필요 → directly
direct(형) → directly(부) / direction(명)
det.tip: direct(직접적인, 형) → directly(곧바로, 부): -ly 접미사로 부사 변환

questions.passage: Little William was surprised at the statement made by the elderly vendor. The vendor insisted that William had to pay because smelling was as good as eating. William thought the vendor's __________ (insist) was unreasonable. He didn't know how merely smelling the meatballs meant that he had to pay for them.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: insist(동사: 주장하다) → insistence(명사: 주장). 소유격 vendor's 뒤에 명사가 필요합니다.
det.analysis:
vendor's + __________ 구조에서 소유격 뒤 명사 필요 → insistence
insist(동) → insistence(명) → insistent(형)
det.tip: insist(주장하다, 동) → insistence(주장, 명): -ence 접미사는 명사화

questions.passage: The shopkeeper angrily shouted, "When did you pay the money? You reached into your pocket but came out empty-handed!" Little William made it clear that he had just paid, reminding the shopkeeper that he had heard the jingle of the coins from his pocket. He added that if smelling is as good as eating, then hearing the sound of the coins should also be as good as receiving them. He smiled proudly and walked home from there, leaving the man __________.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: William의 기지 있는 대답에 상인은 완전히 놀랐습니다(completely surprised).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ completely surprised: 원문 표현 그대로
❌ ① satisfied(만족한): 돈을 못 받았으므로
❌ ② grateful(감사한): 감사할 이유 없음
❌ ③ angry(화난): surprised(놀란)가 원문
det.tip: completely surprised = 완전히 놀란. William의 예상치 못한 대응

questions.passage: He came across the beautiful aroma of some meatballs sold by an elderly vendor just across the road. The smell was so pleasant that little William had to stop by the stand to purchase some meatballs. However, the meatballs didn't have a __________, so he decided to head directly home. Just as little William turned to leave, a firm voice stopped him. It was the elderly vendor who demanded payment.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 미트볼에 표시된 가격(listed price)이 없어서 William은 바로 집으로 가기로 했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① listed price: 원문 표현 그대로
❌ ② cooking recipe(조리법): 가격과 무관
❌ ③ nutrition label(영양 표시): 맥락과 무관
❌ ④ expiration date(유통기한): 구매 결정과 무관
det.tip: listed price = 표시된 가격. 가격이 없어서 구매를 포기한 맥락
